subject: Geo-commitment: scoped failover, subprocessor roster & DPA addendum
messages:
From: Lina Gómez <lina.gomez@novenahealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Data routing assurance + DPA addendum proposal

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novena is interested in moving forward but we need clearer guarantees on two items before we can complete procurement:

1) Territory commitments: we require that PHI-derived model invocations from EU customers remain anchored to EU compute/storage and that any cross-region processing be strictly scoped and time-limited. Specifically, Novena would accept a short, documented failover window for disaster recovery (maximum 72 hours) with audit trails and KMS controls.

2) Subprocessors: please provide the up-to-date roster of subprocessors that might handle telemetry/analytics or disaster-recovery replicas. We need names, locations, and activation triggers.

Attached is a suggested DPA addendum (Novena_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf) with proposed language for the temporary failover carve-out. Can you confirm if Redwood can sign to this language as-is, or if you need changes?

Also loop in your legal/ops folks so we can get a single redline set.

Best,
Lina Gómez
Data Protection Officer
Novena Health

---
Attachment: Novena_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf (pdf, 142 KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gómez <lina.gomez@novenahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing assurance + DPA addendum proposal

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear note and the addendum.

Quick responses up-front:
- We can commit to EU-anchored processing as the default for Novena customer workloads if you pin the tenant to EU in the onboarding configuration.
- We can accept a narrowly scoped failover window for disaster scenarios (we typically operate a 48–96 hour temporary failover option; 72 hours is a reasonable target) but need to capture operational constraints: monitoring triggers, KMS key use, and proof-of-temporary-processing logs.
- Subprocessor roster: we keep a living roster and provide tenant-specific visibility. I will ask Legal for the canonical roster and Ops for the runbook and activation triggers.

@Marissa: can Legal review Novena's addendum and propose any redlines?
@Karthik: can you confirm the telemetry/audit evidence we can produce during a failover (log artifact names/time ranges) and whether we can add a short-term egress guardrail that prevents model weights or permanent backups leaving the EU?

I can set up a 30-minute call this week with Lina and our teams to go through the requirements and expedite to signature. Available Wed/Thu morning PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Lina Gómez <lina.gomez@novenahealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing assurance + DPA addendum proposal

Hi all — reviewed Novena's addendum (high level notes below). I attached a redline separately in DocuSign-friendly form.

Key legal points we should confirm before counter-signing:
- "Temporary failover" definition: propose explicit triggers (region-wide zone outage, provider-contracted maintenance, or security incident). Avoid open-ended language that could be interpreted as normal routing.
- Retention and logs: we can provide a signed snapshot of ephemeral logs showing request timestamps, processing region, and KMS key IDs. However, we cannot alter existing retention policy without product approval; ops, please confirm retention window export capabilities.
- Subprocessor transparency: we will share the live roster link (internal drive). For any non-disclosed subprocessors that would be used in a failover scenario we will require 30-day notice or escrowed compliance attestations.

Suggested edits I will push: tighten "maximum 72 hours" language to "no more than 72 consecutive hours per incident" and require automated notice to Novena's DPO within 4 hours of failover activation.

Docusign link for our proposed counter (pre-fill): https://app.docusign.com/sign/AA12BB34CC
Drive roster (read-only): https://drive.reddemo/novena/subprocessors_roster.xlsx

—Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_Legal_Redline_Novena_Addendum.pdf (pdf, 36 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gómez <lina.gomez@novenahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Jan 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing assurance + DPA addendum proposal

Hi Lina — technical confirmation and operational notes below.

Summary: Redwood can support EU-anchored processing for Novena and a conditional temporary failover for up to 72 consecutive hours per incident with the following controls in place:

Operational controls we will commit to:
- Activation triggers: automated health checks + operator-initiated failover (we will provide a timestamped activation event and rationale).
- Audit evidence: we will provide time-series artifacts (request-level metadata, region tag, KMS key ID, and worker node IDs) in a downloadable archive within 48 hours post-incident.
- KMS: keys for Novena-managed tenants remain in EU KMS; during failover we will use a short-lived key encryption envelope and record the key fingerprint in logs.
- Data handling: no long-term backups or model weights will be persisted outside EU; ephemeral caches may be replicated temporarily and will be purged within 24 hours of failover resolution.
- Subprocessor usage: only listed subprocessors in the shared roster will be allowed; ad-hoc subprocessors require prior approval except for emergency managed DNS/CDN hops which we will disclose within 24 hours.

Attached is an ops runbook snippet that maps triggers to SRE runbook steps: RI-ops-runbook-geo-failover.md. If Novena accepts these controls, Marissa's legal edits can be applied and we can issue the counter via DocuSign.

Action items:
- Lina: please confirm acceptance of the operational controls above and whether Novena needs an on-premises key-holding option (HSM) or if EU KMS with key-fingerprint audit is sufficient.
- Dylan: schedule the 30-minute alignment call once Novena confirms.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI-ops-runbook-geo-failover.md (markdown, 6 KB)
